drivingQuestion: Does a non-kosher egg impart flavor to what it is cooked with, as Rav Naḥman's sixtyfold requirement implies?
outcomeNote: The unit as packeted ends with Rav Idi bar Avin's difficulty standing; Abaye's reply, if any, falls outside these segments.

segments.he: בֵּיצָה בְּשִׁשִּׁים, וְאֵין בֵּיצָה מִן הַמִּנְיָן. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין לְאַבָּיֵי: לְמֵימְרָא דְּיָהֲבָה טַעְמָא? וְהָא אָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי: כִּי מַיָּא דְּבֵיעֵי בְּעָלְמָא!
segments.en: § The Gemara addresses Rav Naḥman’s statement that if the «egg» of a non-kosher bird is cooked with kosher food, it is nullified if the permitted food is «sixty» times its volume, «and the egg» itself «is not counted» in that number, as it cannot nullify itself. «Rav Idi bar Avin said to Abaye:» Is this «to say that» the forbidden egg «imparts flavor» to the food with which it is cooked? «But isn’t» it true that when «people» want to indicate that food is tasteless, they «say:» This is «like mere egg-water?» This indicates that an egg does not impart flavor.

moves.cueHe: ביצה בששים, ואין ביצה מן המנין
moves.summary: The lemma of Rav Naḥman's ruling on the non-kosher egg is re-quoted from the preceding unit.
moves.about: re-quotes Rav Naḥman's clause that a non-kosher egg is nullified in sixty and is not itself counted in the sixty

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב אידי בר אבין לאביי: למימרא דיהבה טעמא?
moves.summary: Does the ruling imply the egg imparts flavor? But people call tasteless food 'mere egg-water'.
moves.about: whether a non-kosher egg imparts flavor at all, given that people call tasteless food 'mere egg-water'

edges.cueHe: אמר ליה רב אידי בר אבין לאביי ... והא אמרי אינשי: כי מיא דביעי בעלמא!
edges.about: whether a non-kosher egg imparts flavor at all, given that people call tasteless food 'mere egg-water'
